name: Browser Use
perceives: DOM plus accessibility tree flattened to indexed interactive elements; screenshots optional
safety: Domain allow lists, placeholders for secrets so the model never sees them, human in the loop hooks
bench: Self reported WebVoyager and Online-Mind2Web scores (vendor judge, not comparable)
lesson: A numbered list of interactive elements is the cheapest grounding; the atlas can emit exactly this list per page.

name: Skyvern
perceives: Screenshots plus DOM element extraction; vision LLM
grounds: Element ids resolved from DOM, vision picks the target
safety: Planner, actor and validator loop; hosted version adds credential vault
bench: Reports WebBench and WebVoyager results on its blog (self reported)
lesson: A validator step that re checks page state after each action catches silent failures.

name: Stagehand
perceives: Accessibility tree and DOM chunks, screenshot optional
safety: Developer scripted, cached actions replay without the LLM
lesson: Three verbs (act, extract, observe) with replay caching is a clean tool surface for an agent.

name: Playwright MCP
perceives: Accessibility snapshot as YAML with ref ids; screenshots as an opt in vision mode
safety: Origin allow and block lists, sandboxed profile, client decides tool approval
lesson: The de facto MCP shape: snapshot tool returns refs, action tools take a ref. Mirror this for the in page MCP.

name: Midscene.js
perceives: Screenshots only (visual grounding model, e.g. Qwen VL or UI-TARS)
safety: Scripts in YAML or JS, reports with replay video
bench: Reports ScreenSpot style grounding results with open models
lesson: One visual loop covers web, Android and iOS; useful as the fallback when the atlas has no id for a target.

name: Nanobrowser
perceives: DOM tree with highlighted indexed elements, optional vision
safety: Runs locally with the user's own keys; planner and navigator agents
lesson: An extension runs inside the user's real logged in session, which is the deployment the console is closest to.

name: OpenManus
perceives: Browser tool built on browser-use plus shell and file tools
lesson: A general agent is mostly tools plus a loop; the atlas is a tool catalog for such a loop.

name: Magentic-UI
perceives: Screenshots with set of marks boxes plus page text
safety: Action guards: user approves risky steps, co planning, plan editing, allow listed sites
bench: Microsoft evaluates on GAIA, WebVoyager and WebGames
lesson: Best published human in the loop UX: plan first, approve per risky step, always interruptible.

name: OpenHands
perceives: Accessibility tree and DOM through BrowserGym
safety: Docker sandbox, confirmation mode for risky commands
bench: SWE-bench for code; WebArena through BrowserGym
lesson: BrowserGym's bid attribute is a prior art for stable element ids.

name: WebVoyager
perceives: Screenshots with set of marks overlay
grounds: Numeric labels drawn on the screenshot
bench: Defines its own 643 task benchmark; original paper 59.1% success; repo last commit 2024-03
lesson: Origin of the set of marks recipe for web agents; stale but historically central.

name: SeeAct
perceives: Screenshot plus ranked DOM candidates
grounds: Two stage: describe action, then ground to candidate element
lesson: Separating what to do from which element is a useful split that the atlas can serve (the element side).

name: Amazon Nova Act
perceives: Screenshots and page state
grounds: Pixel and element targets chosen by the Nova model
safety: Developer scripted act() steps, human handoff hooks
bench: Amazon reports its own reliability numbers
lesson: Small atomic act() steps are more reliable than free running goals.

name: Anthropic computer use
perceives: Screenshots
acts: OS input injection (xdotool in a Docker X11 desktop) via computer tool actions
safety: Run in a VM or container, prompt injection classifiers, user confirmation for consequential actions per docs
bench: Claimed top OSWorld results across model generations; verify on the official OSWorld board
lesson: Reference loop: screenshot, model, action, screenshot. The atlas adds ids so the model need not guess pixels.

name: Claude in Chrome
perceives: Page content, accessibility structure and screenshots
safety: Per site permissions, confirmation for high risk actions; pilot cut injection attack success from 23.6% to 11.2%; a 2026 extension messaging flaw (fixed May 2026) shows the extension itself is attack surface
bench: Vendor reports injection rates, not task benchmarks
lesson: Permissions per origin plus confirm on high risk is the shipped norm; lock down who may message the agent.

name: OpenAI CUA / Operator / ChatGPT agent
perceives: Screenshots
acts: Virtual mouse and keyboard in a remote browser
safety: Asks before login and payments, watch mode on sensitive sites, takeover mode without screenshots. Help center now reports ChatGPT agent mode as no longer available (replaced by ChatGPT Work); Operator was retired in 2025
bench: Launch figures: OSWorld 38.1%, WebArena 58.1%, WebVoyager 87% (OpenAI, Jan 2025); Online-Mind2Web 61.3% in the independent paper
lesson: Takeover mode that stops screenshotting during user input is a privacy pattern worth copying.

name: Gemini computer use
perceives: Screenshots
acts: Client executes predefined actions via Playwright
safety: Per action safety_decision: allowed, require_confirmation or blocked; client must ask the user
bench: Vendor reports Online-Mind2Web and WebVoyager at launch
lesson: A server side per action risk label the client must honour is a clean confirmation contract.

name: UI-TARS
perceives: Screenshots only, end to end VLM with chain of thought
acts: Emits actions executed by a harness (pyautogui, ADB, browser)
bench: OSWorld, AndroidWorld, ScreenSpot, WebVoyager reported in the UI-TARS 1.5 release (OSWorld about 42% at 100 steps, per the release)
lesson: End to end pixel models are strong but depend on screenshots; repo archived 2026-01, so check forks.

name: UI-TARS Desktop / Agent TARS
perceives: Screenshots (GUI mode), DOM and MCP tools (Agent TARS)
acts: Native input injection, browser control, MCP
voice: Early versions let the user dictate tasks (voice entry); check current build
safety: Local operator mode, user can pause; repo archived 2026-10
lesson: Hybrid GUI plus MCP tool use in one agent is the direction the field took.

name: Agent S (Simular)
perceives: Screenshot plus accessibility tree, separate grounding model
acts: pyautogui style OS input, code agent
grounds: Pixel coordinates from a grounding model
safety: Local code execution is a risk the docs flag
bench: README: Agent S3 72.60% on OSWorld (above the 72% human baseline); Sai 73% on OSWorld 2.0 (vendor claims)
lesson: Split planner and grounding model is the winning design; best open OSWorld result.

name: OmniParser
perceives: Screenshot parsed to boxes and captions (icon detector plus captioner plus OCR)
acts: None (parser only, used with any agent)
grounds: Element ids over detected boxes (set of marks)
bench: V2: 39.5% on ScreenSpot Pro with GPT-4o (README)
lesson: Turns any pixels into a structured element list; the atlas does the same job from the DOM for free.

name: Microsoft UFO
perceives: Windows UI Automation tree plus screenshots (hybrid)
acts: UIA control patterns, Win32 and COM APIs, plus mouse and keyboard
grounds: Control ids from UIA, with vision fallback
safety: Safeguards and approval for sensitive actions, documented
lesson: Prefer the accessibility API and fall back to vision; native APIs beat clicks when they exist.

name: Self-Operating Computer
perceives: Screenshots, optional grid overlay, OCR and set of marks modes
voice: Optional voice mode (-voice flag) transcribes a spoken objective, then runs the loop; no barge in
safety: Press Ctrl+C to stop; no confirmations
lesson: Voice only sets the goal; the loop afterwards is silent. A thin precedent for A plus B.

name: Open Interpreter
license: Apache-2.0 (as returned by GitHub API; earlier AGPL)
perceives: Screenshots in OS mode, plus code output
acts: Runs generated code locally; OS mode uses pyautogui style control
safety: Asks before running each code block unless auto_run is on
lesson: Confirm before execute is the oldest safety UX in this space.

name: trycua Cua
perceives: Screenshots from macOS, Linux or Windows VMs
safety: Agents run in isolated VMs, not on the user's desktop
bench: Ships cua-bench and reports OSWorld and ScreenSpot with several models
lesson: Run the agent in a sandbox and give it the page's own tool surface; separates risk from capability.

name: E2B Surf
perceives: Screenshots of a cloud desktop
acts: xdotool in an E2B desktop sandbox
voice: Demo accepts microphone input (check repo); text first
lesson: Disposable cloud desktops make 'undo' trivial; the atlas console is a safe sandbox by construction.

name: OpenAdapt
kind: open record and replay with AI
perceives: Screenshots, window and accessibility metadata, input events
grounds: Element and pixel via a VLM
safety: Local data scrubbing (PII) is a stated feature
lesson: Recording human demos yields training data; the console's event stream could do the same for page controls.

name: OpenCUA
perceives: Screenshots
bench: README: OpenCUA-72B reaches 45.0% on OSWorld-Verified, 60.8% on ScreenSpot-Pro
lesson: Open data (AgentNet) plus open weights make a fully local agent possible.

name: ShowUI
perceives: Screenshots with UI guided token selection (2B model)
bench: ScreenSpot grounding; Mind2Web and AITW navigation
lesson: Small local models can ground well; relevant for in browser inference later.

name: CogAgent
perceives: Screenshots, high resolution
lesson: Early open high resolution GUI VLM; shows resolution matters for small controls.

name: Open-AutoGLM (Phone Agent)
perceives: Screenshots
grounds: Pixel coordinates from the AutoGLM-Phone model
voice: Voice or text task in the product line; the open repo is text driven
safety: Human takeover for logins and captchas, sensitive action confirmation
lesson: Hand control back to the human for logins; same rule applies to a console that has sign in flows.

name: Mobile-Agent (X-PLUG)
perceives: Screenshots, OCR and icon detection in early versions; end to end GUI-Owl in v3
bench: AndroidWorld and AndroidLab (v3 reports strong open model results)
lesson: Shows the progression: tool pipelines (OCR plus detectors) then end to end models.

name: AppAgent
perceives: Screenshots with numbered overlays built from the Android XML UI tree
lesson: Exploration phase writes per app documentation the agent reads later: the atlas is that documentation, made ahead of time.

name: Mobilerun (formerly droidrun)
perceives: Accessibility tree via a Portal app plus screenshots
acts: ADB and the Portal accessibility service
safety: Self hosted device, optional cloud phones
bench: Vendor reports AndroidWorld results on its blog
lesson: Accessibility tree first, screenshots second; ships an agent skill so coding agents can drive phones.

name: Minitap mobile-use
perceives: UI hierarchy plus screenshots
bench: README claims 100% on AndroidWorld (vendor claim, independent run not found)
lesson: Multi agent planner, cortex and executor split; treat headline benchmark numbers as vendor claims.

name: Microsoft Copilot Studio computer use
perceives: Screenshots and reasoning traces captured per step
acts: Virtual machine or hosted browser input
safety: Makers review screenshots and reasoning, admin controls; reported generally available (secondary sources)
lesson: Audit trail of screenshot plus reasoning per step is what enterprises expect from agent actions.

name: UiPath agentic automation (UI agent)
perceives: UI selectors from its automation library plus screenshots for the computer use path
acts: Selector based UI automation, with LLM planned steps
lesson: RPA's selector idea (durable ids, not coordinates) is what an atlas id gives the model.

name: Robocorp (Sema4.ai)
perceives: DOM, window trees
lesson: Open RPA stacks reuse locator strategies; useful reference for selector fallbacks.

name: OSWorld / OSWorld-Verified
perceives: 369 tasks across real Ubuntu, Windows, macOS apps
bench: Human baseline about 72%. Trackers (Oct 2026) report top agents between 85% and 90%, with different setups, so use the official board for comparison
lesson: The yardstick desktop agents are judged on.

name: WebArena
perceives: 812 tasks on self hosted sites
bench: Operator launch figure 58.1%; June 2026 paper reports 56.3% with open weights
lesson: Self hosted fake sites give repeatable web evals; the console could host its own task set.

name: AndroidWorld
perceives: 116 tasks across 20 apps on an emulator, with accessibility tree access
bench: Scores vary by board and metric; vendor claims range from about 75% to above 90%
lesson: Task generators with programmatic rewards are the right way to score page controls too.

name: Pipecat
perceives: Audio frames (and video)
acts: Function calls to your code; transports WebRTC (Daily), WebSocket, telephony
voice: Cascaded STT, LLM, TTS or speech to speech services; pluggable VAD (Silero) and smart turn model; interruptions cancel TTS frames
lesson: Frame pipeline with interruption frames is the clearest open design for barge in.

name: LiveKit Agents
perceives: Audio, video, text over WebRTC rooms
acts: Function tools, RPC to frontend participants
voice: STT, LLM, TTS or realtime models; VAD plus open weights turn detector model; interruption handling; MCP support
lesson: Frontend RPC from agent to browser participant is exactly the voice to in page action path.

name: OpenAI Realtime API (gpt-realtime)
perceives: Audio, text, images
acts: Function calling over WebRTC, WebSocket, SIP
voice: Speech to speech; server VAD or semantic VAD; barge in truncates output; async function calls
safety: Developer controlled; ephemeral client secrets for browsers
lesson: Ephemeral keys plus client side tool execution lets the browser run the tools.

name: Gemini Live API
perceives: Audio, video and screen share frames
voice: Native audio speech to speech over WebSocket; built in VAD and interruption; ephemeral tokens for browsers
lesson: Sibling session picked this for the AI page; screen share plus tools is the only A plus B hosted API.

name: Vapi
perceives: Phone and web audio
acts: Server URL webhooks for tool calls, custom LLM endpoints
voice: Cascaded STT, LLM, TTS with provider choice; interruption and endpointing settings; can use OpenAI Realtime
lesson: Tool calls as webhooks are simple but add latency; a client side tool avoids the round trip.

name: Retell AI
perceives: Phone and web audio
acts: Functions via webhooks; custom LLM over WebSocket
voice: Cascaded with a proprietary turn taking model tuned for barge in
lesson: Dedicated turn taking model is the differentiator vendors compete on.

name: ElevenLabs Agents
perceives: Audio, text
acts: Client tools (run in the browser), server tools, system tools, MCP servers
voice: Cascaded with proprietary turn taking model; per tool interruption modes (lock interruptions during critical tools); skip_turn tool
lesson: Per tool interruption policy (do not let barge in cancel a destructive action mid flight) is a smart safety hook.

name: Ultravox
perceives: Audio goes straight into the LLM (no separate STT)
voice: Speech in, text out; separate TTS; hosted API adds turn handling
lesson: Skipping STT saves latency and keeps tone; text out still needs TTS.

name: Moshi
perceives: Audio, full duplex
voice: Full duplex speech to speech, listens while it speaks so barge in is native
lesson: Full duplex removes turn detection entirely but lacks tools today.

name: Kyutai Unmute
perceives: Audio
acts: Wraps any text LLM; no tool layer documented
voice: Open STT and TTS around an LLM, semantic VAD, interruptions
lesson: Fully open cascade for self hosting.

name: OpenAI Whisper
perceives: Audio files (not streaming by itself)
voice: STT only; streaming needs wrappers (faster-whisper, whisper.cpp)
lesson: The default offline STT; relevant for a local mode.

name: Talon Voice
perceives: Active window, accessibility tree on macOS and Windows, app context for scoped commands
acts: OS input injection plus accessibility actions; Python scripts
grounds: Command grammar plus on screen labels
voice: Own speech engine, command grammar (not an LLM); noise and eye tracking input
lesson: Deterministic grammars are fast and safe; an LLM should map free speech onto such a grammar, not replace it.

name: Cursorless
perceives: Editor text, with spoken hat marks over tokens
grounds: Colored hats over tokens: spoken ids
voice: Runs on Talon (or other speech tools)
lesson: Spoken hat marks are the best precedent for 'say the id of the thing'.

name: macOS Voice Control
perceives: Accessibility tree of the front app
voice: On device speech recognition, commands plus dictation; no LLM planning
safety: Built in; confirmations for destructive ones
lesson: Show numbers / show names overlays are the template for voice grounding on any UI.

name: Windows Voice Access
perceives: UI Automation tree
voice: On device speech; newer builds add natural language commands
lesson: Same overlay idea; both desktop OS vendors converged on it.

name: Android Voice Access
perceives: Accessibility tree
lesson: Accessibility service plus numbered overlays is the mobile twin of the same pattern.

name: Rabbit r1 LAM playground
perceives: Screenshots of a cloud browser (Rabbit says its playground is based on WebVoyager)
voice: Push to talk voice prompt on device, cloud STT and LLM; no barge in documented
safety: Teach mode scoped per site; CAPTCHAs and logins limited; CEO admitted launch overpromised
lesson: Cautionary tale: voice front end over a weak action layer fails on reliability, not UX.

name: Open Interpreter 01
perceives: Audio in, plus whatever the interpreter sees
acts: Runs generated code on the host
voice: Push to talk STT, LLM, TTS streamed over a WebSocket server
safety: Asks before running code unless auto run
lesson: A+B in one open repo; last commit 2024-11, so a reference, not a base.

name: Apple App Intents / Siri
perceives: App declared actions, entities and on screen content
voice: On device and cloud speech; Siri LLM features reported
safety: Intents carry confirmation and authentication requirements
lesson: Apps declare typed actions for the assistant: this is what the atlas manifest can become for a web page.

name: Home Assistant Assist
perceives: Entity registry states
grounds: Entity ids and aliases (names resolved by exposed entity list)
voice: Wyoming protocol: wake word, STT, intent or LLM, TTS satellites; local or cloud
safety: Only exposed entities can be controlled; user chooses exposure
lesson: The exposure list (user picks what the assistant may control) is a strong model for per site agent scopes.

name: Willow
perceives: Microphone on ESP32 devices
voice: On device wake word and VAD, streaming STT server, TTS
lesson: Edge wake word plus local server is the privacy preserving shape.

name: Leon
perceives: Text and voice
voice: STT and TTS options, skill routing
lesson: Skill registry mirrors a tool catalog.

name: OpenVoiceOS
perceives: Audio
voice: Wake word, STT, intents, TTS plugins; Mycroft successor (mycroft-core archived)
lesson: Plugin architecture for every stage.
